newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT - Tyco on American Standard offer.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - Tyco on American Standard offer.

text.p: Tyco International Ltd issued the following statement regarding its offer to American Standard Companies Inc.
Tyco International Provides Contents of Letter Proposing Business Combination with American Standard

EXETER, N.H., Jan. 13 /PRNewswire/ -- Responding to numerous inquiries stemming from a story in today's Wall Street Journal, Tyco made public the contents of a December 5, 1996 letter outlining a proposed $50 per share business combination with American Standard.

Tyco's proposal was rejected in a fax received on the following day, December 6, 1996, stating, in effect, that since American Standard was not for sale there would be no point in having any discussion of Tyco's proposal:
(Tyco International Ltd. Letterhead)
"December 5, 1996
Mr. Emmanuel A. Kampouris
Chairman, President and CEO
American Standard Companies Inc.
One Centennial Avenue
Piscataway, New Jersey 08855-6820
Dear Mr. Kampouris:

We continue to believe that there are many advantages that would result from a combination of our two companies. Both American Standard and Tyco are worldwide, world-class manufacturers with strong leadership positions in each of their businesses. Our companies could benefit significantly through a business combination. For example:
-- American Standard's plumbing products business and Tyco's flow control operations share many customers. The advantages of a single distribution system for both businesses is obvious.

-- Tyco has a worldwide presence outside the U.S., with market leadership positions in Europe, Asia and Australia in fire protection and building security systems. A combination with Trane would create the world's largest single source for the design, sale, installation and service of air conditioning, fire protection and security systems and would allow for greater pull-through of product.

-- American Standard has a significant presence and strong relationships in China. A combination of the two companies would provide a significant opportunity to expand the market for Tyco's products in that country.

We are proposing a combination of two outstanding well-run companies, each with excellent prospects for growth, through a merger of equals. Based on our analysis, we believe such a combination would provide many opportunities for sales growth and would produce annual cost savings synergies of a minimum of $150-200 million.
We are proposing a business combination of the two companies on the following terms:

-- Shareholders of American Standard would receive a purchase price of $50.00 per share of American Standard, either in Tyco stock or cash or any combination thereof at their election, except that a minimum of 50 percent of the total consideration would be in Tyco stock. This percentage could increase if American Standard shareholders so elect. We expect the transaction to be tax-free for Tyco stock received;

-- The managements of the two companies would be combined drawing on the strength of both companies. We have no doubt that a large part of the success of American Standard is attributable to you and your management team. We look forward to getting your views on a management structure that would include your enthusiastic participation;
-- The combined company's Board of Directors would be expanded to consist of twelve persons, the eight existing Tyco directors and four individuals from American Standard's board;
-- The principal offices of the combined companies would be located in the New York metropolitan area and would not require the relocation of executive personnel; and
-- Both American Standard and Tyco would be incorporated in the new name of the combined company.
JP Morgan has committed to lead the financing arrangements required for the transaction as well as any refinancing needs.

Based on our analysis, we are confident that the transaction would be accretive to the earnings per share of Tyco, both in the short term as well as the long term. We believe a combination of our two companies would provide significantly greater opportunity for enhanced shareholder value than either company could achieve by itself.

As a first step, we would very much like you and your management team to learn more about our operations and prospects and to review our analysis of the benefits and synergies that would result from a combination of our two companies.
Very truly yours,
TYCO INTERNATIONAL LTD.
L. Dennis Kozlowski
Chairman of the Board and Chief Executive Officer
cc: American Standard Board of Directors"

Tyco International is a worldwide manufacturer with strong leadership positions in disposable medical products, packaging materials, flow control products, electrical and electronic components and is the world's largest manufacturer and provider of fire and safety systems and services. The Company operates in more than 50 countries around the world and has revenues in excess of $6 billion.
